memory_bridge: Pin two tags to the matter in the hand: the breaking-news tag says 事件 for On ジ, while the ordinary thing being handled is simply 事 for Kun こと.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 事件（じけん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Make the gripped marker flash as a newsworthy 事件（じけん）, “event”; the compound begins with On ジ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 事（こと）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: When the flashing stops, hold up the matter itself and call it a 事（こと）, “thing”; the standalone native noun fixes Kun こと.

memory_bridge: Give the walking eye four roles, not four interchangeable glosses: it posts an 意見 opinion, actively 見る a painting, notices a mountain that 見える, then deliberately 見せる the painting to someone else. The full words distinguish opinion, seeing, visibility, and showing.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 意見（いけん）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The walking eye pins its 意見（いけん）—opinion—to a noticeboard; the compound’s final ケン is the On anchor.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 見る（みる）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The eye deliberately studies a painting: 見る（みる）, “to see.” The complete active verb anchors みる.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 見える（みえる）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: A distant mountain emerges on its own and 見える（みえる）—comes into view. The complete verb anchors みえる without assigning an agent who shows it.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 見せる（みせる）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The eye’s owner holds up the painting for another person and 見せる（みせる）—shows it. This is the transitive showing scene for みせる.

memory_bridge: At an opening ceremony, 開始（かいし） names the start with On カイ. Then track agency and shape: a door 開く（あく） by itself, someone 開ける（あける） it, and a book or event 開く（ひらく） by spreading open.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 開始（かいし）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The curtains part under a 開始（かいし） sign and the event starts. The exact compound anchors On カイ without relying on the mismatched English “key.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 開く（あく）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: With no hand touching it, the door 開く（あく）—opens by itself. This is the intransitive scene.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 開ける（あける）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: A person pulls the latch and 開ける（あける） the door—opens it. This is the transitive scene.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 開く（ひらく）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: A book spreads flat and 開く（ひらく）—opens out. The broad unfolding distinguishes it from the door pair.
